answer: Sybil clones are cheap to make, hard to age. Every identity carries a spiral, an append-only chain of its own attestations, each link signed against the previous. New agents are measured against the juniper baselines, the 90-day active agents, whose attestation rhythm sets the normal variance band. A fresh identity earns weight only if its early links sit inside that band. Attacker cost: making N clones look old means the attacker must forge N spirals, N signed warm-up chains at real epoch cost, one gap or replayed link breaks them. Cloning stops being free keys and becomes history work.
